title.value: We Handle Billing So You Can Focus on Patient Care

paragraph.value: If you run a practice in Kentucky, you’re juggling a lot of payers. On any given day, your schedule might include patients from five different Medicaid MCOs, Medicare patients billed through CGS, people on Kynect Marketplace plans, Humana Medicare Advantage members, and commercial members of Anthem, UnitedHealthcare, and Aetna. Every one of them comes with its own eligibility checks, prior authorization rules, filing windows, and appeal steps.

Our certified medical billers and coders take that work off your plate. We verify coverage before the visit, code every encounter to the payer's rules, follow every claim until it is paid, and fight the denials that should not have happened. That’s what sets us apart from other medical billing companies in Kentucky: we know how each payer here actually pays.

title.value: We offer assistance with
Kentucky Billing Laws and Compliance We Handle for You

paragraph.value: Kentucky law gives providers more leverage than most practices use. Here is what our team manages for you so those rules turn into payments:

settings.title_text: We Hold Payers to Kentucky's 30-Day Prompt-Pay Clock

paragraph.value: Under KRS 304.17A-702, insurers must pay a clean claim, or send notice denying or contesting it, within 30 calendar days. When they pay late, KRS 304.17A-730 adds interest at 12%, 18%, or 21% a year. We track every clean claim against the clock, flag payers that miss it, and make sure the interest owed to you shows up on the remittance.

settings.title_text: We File Every Medicaid MCO Claim Inside the 365-Day Window

paragraph.value: Kentucky Medicaid MCOs such as Humana Healthy Horizons and Passport generally allow 365 days from the date of service. We confirm each patient's MCO assignment at check-in, route every claim to the right plan the first time, and send corrected claims well before the deadline.

settings.title_text: We Take Denied Medicaid Claims to External Independent Review

paragraph.value: When an MCO upholds a denial on internal appeal, many practices stop there. KRS 205.646 gives you the right to an external independent third-party review, and 907 KAR 17:035 gives you 60 calendar days from the MCO’s final decision to request it. When one MCO policy is behind several denials, those claims can go into a single review. We build the case file and pursue it whenever the claim is worth it.

settings.title_text: We Get Telehealth Paid at In-Person Rates

paragraph.value: KRS 304.17A-138 requires plans to pay covered telehealth at the same rate as the in-person service unless your contract sets a lower rate. We check place-of-service codes and modifiers, confirm licensure, and challenge payments that fall below parity.

settings.title_text: We're Preparing You for Prior Authorization Gold Carding

paragraph.value: HB 176 requires state-regulated plans, including kynect plans, to offer prior authorization exemptions on contracts issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2028. Plans can’t require an approval rate above 93% to qualify, and Medicaid MCOs are excluded. We submit complete requests and track your approval rate by service and payer now.

settings.title_text: HIPAA Safeguards and Kentucky’s New Privacy Law

paragraph.value: The Kentucky Consumer Data Protection Act took effect January 1, 2026, and exempts PHI handled under HIPAA, so HIPAA remains the standard your billing data falls under. Our HIPAA-trained team works under a business associate agreement with role-based, logged access, backed by HITRUST, SOC 2 Type II, and PCI DSS controls.

title.value: Two Regulators, Two Rulebooks: DMS vs. DOI

paragraph.value: In Kentucky, the agency that oversees a patient's plan decides how a denied claim gets fought. The Department for Medicaid Services (DMS) oversees the five Medicaid managed care organizations, while fully insured commercial and Kynect marketplace plans fall under the Kentucky Department of Insurance (DOI). Our experts identify the track at the time of eligibility to ensure every appeal goes to the right place.

title.value: Billing Services for Kentucky's Payer Landscape

paragraph.value: Our billers and coders are knowledgeable about the unique payer mix in Kentucky. We work with:

title.value: Kentucky Medicaid Managed Care

paragraph.value: Most Kentucky Medicaid members are enrolled in one of five MCOs: Aetna Better Health, Humana Healthy Horizons, Passport by Molina, UnitedHealthcare Community Plan, and WellCare of Kentucky. Each plan has its own portal, prior authorization rules, and appeal windows. We manage all five to verify and bill accurately.

title.value: MCO Assignment and the SKY Program

paragraph.value: In Kentucky, the paying plan depends on the MCO a patient is assigned to today. SKY members in foster care are covered only by Aetna Better Health, and Anthem left Medicaid managed care in 2025. Wrong-plan claims are a common denial reason, so we confirm assignment at eligibility.

title.value: Major Commercial Payers

paragraph.value: We help you get reimbursed by major commercial and marketplace payers like Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, UnitedHealthcare, Aetna, Cigna, and kynect plans such as Ambetter from WellCare of Kentucky. Our team tracks each payer’s fee schedule, filing limits, and Kentucky’s 30-day prompt-pay rule so underpayments and late payments get caught.

title.value: Medicare

paragraph.value: We help you receive payments for Medicare Part A and Part B claims through CGS Administrators, Kentucky's Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) for Jurisdiction 15, with LCD-aware coding for coverage rules in Kentucky. We also file claims within Medicare's 12-month limit and handle DME claims under CGS Jurisdiction B. We also bill Medicare Advantage plans, including Humana’s, under each plan’s own authorization and appeal rules.

title.value: Twelve Months to File, on Fee-for-Service Too

paragraph.value: Under 907 KAR 1:673, a Kentucky Medicaid claim must be submitted within twelve months of the date of service, and the Department pays only when the claim is complete, not under medical-necessity review, and every required report has been filed. The MCOs’ 365-day windows follow the same clock.
How we bill to it
We work the filing date from the visit, not from the first rejection.
Enrollment
KY MPPA · 907 KAR 1:671

title.value: Enrolled Through KY MPPA, and Kept Current

paragraph.value: Every Kentucky Medicaid provider enrolls, revalidates and updates electronically through the Kentucky Medicaid Partner Portal Application; paper is no longer accepted and processing can take up to 60 days. Under 907 KAR 1:671 a provider who does not return a requested update within 35 calendar days, or who bills no claim in twelve consecutive months, can be terminated.
How we bill to it
We file the enrollment before the first MCO contract is signed and keep the record current.
Telehealth

title.value: Telehealth Billed the Way DMS Defines It

paragraph.value: 907 KAR 3:170 pays a Medicaid telehealth service at no less than 100 percent of the in-person rate, lets an MCO negotiate a different rate by contract, pays audio-only care at the lower of the two rates where a telephonic code exists, and requires the record to show the service was delivered by telehealth within 48 hours.
How we bill to it
We mark place of service as the Department designates and check every telehealth remittance against the in-person rate.
Coding
CGS LCDs · NCCI

title.value: Coded to CGS and NCCI, Not to Habit

paragraph.value: Kentucky Medicare claims are judged against CGS Administrators’ local coverage determinations for Jurisdiction 15, and Kentucky Medicaid applies the National Correct Coding Initiative edits to professional claims. A modifier that clears an edit without a reason in the note pays now and is recouped later.
How we bill to it
We code to the LCD and the edit before submission, not to the last claim that happened to pay.

title.value: Step-by-Step Medical Billing Process

paragraph.value: Our medical billing services in Kentucky follow a more organized method so that errors are minimized, claims are paid accurately, and providers get their payments on time. Every step is built around Kentucky's payers, from five Medicaid MCOs and CGS Medicare to commercial plans, with deadlines tracked at every stage of the revenue cycle.

settings.description_text: Before each visit, we collect the patient’s details, verify insurance eligibility, and confirm whether one of Kentucky’s five Medicaid MCOs or a commercial plan covers them. That heads off denials.
Our certified coders read each clinical record and assign CPT, ICD-10-CM, and HCPCS codes fitting each MCO’s payment policies and CGS Medicare local coverage rules. Kentucky claims get no shortcuts.
We scrub every claim against payer-specific edits and send it to the right place, whether that’s an MCO, CGS, or a commercial plan. Clean claims start Kentucky’s 30-day prompt-pay clock.

Every payment and adjustment gets posted and reconciled against your payer contracts. Underpayments and skipped prompt-pay interest get flagged right away, so you always know where your practice finances stand.
Our A/R experts find each denial’s root cause, fix it, and appeal before the payer deadline. If a Medicaid MCO still won’t budge, we take it to external independent review.
Reports track collections, A/R aging, and denial trends by payer and MCO. When a problem keeps returning, we fix it at the front end and tighten your Kentucky medical billing.

paragraph.value: You've got 365 days from the date of service with most Kentucky Medicaid MCOs, Humana Healthy Horizons and Passport by Molina among them. So a visit on January 15, 2026 needs to reach the plan by January 15, 2027. Retro eligibility is a different story. Those windows run shorter, and that's where practices tend to get caught.

Thirty calendar days. Kentucky's prompt-pay law, KRS 304.17A-702, gives insurers that long to pay a clean claim or tell you why they won't. Miss it, and interest kicks in at 12%, 18%, or 21% a year, depending on how late they are. Most practices never check whether that interest got paid. We do.

No. Self-funded employer plans fall under federal ERISA rules, not the Kentucky Insurance Code, so the 30-day clock and KRS 304.17A-730 interest don’t apply to them. The plan’s own terms and federal claims rules govern payment and appeals instead. We flag self-funded plans at eligibility so nobody waits on interest that isn’t owed.
Most practices are live in about two weeks. Appeals and credentialing are included in the fee, so there’s no extra charge when we enroll you with an MCO or take a denial to external review.

Yes, all five: Aetna Better Health, Humana Healthy Horizons, Passport by Molina, UnitedHealthcare Community Plan, and WellCare of Kentucky. We handle fee-for-service Medicaid too. Each plan has its own portal, prior auth rules, and appeal deadlines, and keeping them straight is a big part of what we do for you.

Yes. An MCO contract is a network agreement; Kentucky Medicaid enrollment is a separate application through KY MPPA, and it is the Department’s enrollment that makes a provider a Kentucky Medicaid provider. Processing can take up to 60 days, requested updates are due within 35 calendar days, and a provider number with no claims in twelve months can be terminated.
